NVIDIA Corp (NVDA.O) Sales Acceleration into 2026; TP to \$270; Maintain Buy CITI'S TAKE NVDA stock was +5% after market after guiding Jan-Q to \$65B sales above market’s \~\$63B expectations. With TSMC CoWoS wafer capacity now expected to grow to 1.2M next year, we see a path for Nvidia to accelerate + upside prior \$500B+ 2025/26 data center sales as recent Anthropic and Middle East partnerships are incremental. Three key highlights from the call: a) CEO Jensen believes we are not in an AI bubble as three separate platforms accelerated compute, Gen AI, and Agentic AI collide; b) Open AI and Anthropic its two investment partnerships are most successful AI companies in terms of consumption; and c) despite rising input costs gross margins can hold mid-70s. Estimate Changes — We revise FY27/FY28 sales by 19%/26% reflecting what we now expect to be a re-accelerated DC sales backed by better-than expected Blackwell and Rubin demand visibility. Though pushing down our FY27E/FY28E non-GAAP GM estimates to 75%/75.3% from prior 76%/76.1% respectively, our FY27/28 EPS estimates go up by 12%/19% to \$8.10 and \$10.08, respectively. We raise our TP to \$270 on consistent 30x P/E times revised CY27 EPS power of \~\$10 discounted back. We move our valuation basis to CY27 from prior CY26 to reflect increasing AI spend visibility. Citi AI GPU Model — We revise our GPU units’ estimates following more datapoints indicating a higher supply of CoWoS for Blackwell and Rubin (see Citi TSMC analyst Laura Chen’s note). While we kept our FY2026 units of 7.1M unchanged we raise our FY2027 units to 10.2M units (+44% Y/Y vs prior 8.7M). We expect Blackwell and Rubin between C2025 and C2026 to be 16.2M up from 14.2M. Backed by units’ upticks and favorable product mix, we estimate FY2027 sales reaching \$269B (up 19% from our prior \$225B estimate). Our GPU sales revisions of \$44B reflect mostly our revisions to our overall NVDA units’ assumption but also to our larger Blackwell and Rubin combined. We update our Blackwell and Rubin combined sales from \$358B to \$417B (+16%) during the C2025-C2026 timeframe. We expect sales of AI GPUs to represent on average high 80% to 90% of total NVDA data center sales in FY2026-FY2027, with the remaining being comprised primarily of networking (Ethernet and InfiniBand), standalone CPUs, and software/services offerings.

NVIDIA Corp (NVDA.O) 20 November 2025 Citi Research 2

NVIDIA Oct-Q Review
I- Results and Outlook
NVDA reported Oct-Q revs/non-GAAP EPS (ex-SBC) of \$57B/\$1.30 vs. our \$56.8B/\$1.29 and Street’s (FactSet) \$54.9B/\$1.26 (ex-SBC). The company’s Data Center revenue grew 25% sequentially, with the company previously announcing shipping 6M units from January to October and signaling production of GB200/GB300 being at full ramp given its technology leadership (see latest MLPerf results). In fact, Jensen Huang (CEO) described demand for Blackwell as “off the charts” with cloud GPUs “sold out”. NVDA guided Jan-Q revenue to \$65B (at MP) vs. our \$62.6B and Street’s \$62.2B. Looking at other metrics, Oct-Q non-GAAP GM (ex-SBC) came in at 73.6% below Citi’s 74% and Street’s 73.9%. That said, NVDA is guiding GM to grow further with Jan-Q’s Non-GAAP GM (ex-SBC) reaching 75% (at MP), which is in line with Citi and Street expectations.
Going by segments:
Data Center (DC) sales grew by 25% Q/Q (vs. Citi’s/Street’s +24%/+19%) as discussed at GTC DC, Blackwell ramp continues to beat expectations. Networking (\$8.2B) came significantly higher than the \$5B-\$7B expectations. With the transition from Hopper to Blackwell complete, Blackwell accounted for approximately 90%+ of the \$43B in quarterly Compute sales up from \~84% last quarter. Notably management discussed GB300 representing 2/3 of the compute sales as it crossed over GB200. The GB300 platform likely surpassed its previously discussed 1k per week run rate across racks. Although already above expectations, we expect this run-rate to further increase as companies such as Anthropic are added to GB300 list of customers. The Networking business resumed its growth and was up 13% QoQ, fueled by the Blackwell ramp as well as continued growth in Spectrum-X and NVLink.

Pivoting to China DC sales, NVDA was as expected unable to ship much H20 in the third quarter due to the US export controls (\$50M). Management continues to bake in zero China H20 sales.
Gaming revenue was down 1% Q/Q (vs. Citi’s/Street’s +1%/+2%) but up 30% Y/Y. The segment represented \~7% of sales this quarter. This was driven by the ramp of Blackwell GeForce GPUs amid an increased supply availability. We continue to model the segment being mostly in lockstep with notebook seasonality thus down sequentially in Jan-Q. We estimate with supply easing in gaming, NVDA will accelerate the shipment of its next Gen GeForce RTX AI PC. On-device AI front, NVDA discussed RTX GPUs as the best platform.
Pro Visualization revenue was up 26% QoQ (vs. Citi’s/Street’s +10%/flat), the segment reached now \$760M in sales. NVDA sees strong demand with DGX Spark being the key driver for growth. On top of DGX Spark, we estimate that DGX Station which management talked about its deployment in 2H later this year, will likely contribute further to growth. We estimate that the segment to now be more tied to AI than gaming thus while we suspect the larger portion of the segment will reflect gaming seasonality, we estimate the rapid growth of DGX will help generate moderate growth in Jan-Q despite two consecutive 15%+ sequential growth quarters. We model 2% growth in Jan-Q.
Auto sales rose modestly by 1% Q/Q (vs. Citi’s/Street’s +9%/+5%). NVDA pursues shipments of NVIDIA Thor SoC, the successor to Oren. Thor's arrival coincides with the industry's accelerating shift to vision language model architecture generative AI and higher levels of autonomy. To us it is clear, NVDA is seeing growth in in-car chip demand as some customers are starting to launch L3 which requires more advanced algorithms as well as larger models. Outside the vehicle they are seeing a large opportunity with, for instance, their digital twin offering with Omniverse used by OEMs to test their AV applications. Toyota, the world’s largest automaker, will build its next-generation vehicles on NVIDIA DRIVE AGX, running the safetycertified NVIDIA DriveOS operating system. Today NVDA announced end-to-end autonomous vehicle platform NVIDIA Drive Hyperion has passed industry safety assessments like TÜV SUD and TUV Rheinland, 2 of the industry's foremost authorities for automotive grade safety and cybersecurity. This quarter NVDA discussed its partnership with Uber to scale the world's largest Level 4 ready autonomous fleet built on the new NVIDIA Hyperion L4 robotaxi reference architecture. We think, NVDA’s new 1-year cadence will deliver new products with new architectures that can accelerate adoption by auto OEMs. Management previously discussed its Auto total sales (DC + Auto) to reach \$5B in FY2026. With 7% QoQ growth in Jan-Q we model the auto segment to reach \$2.4B with the remaining \$2.6B+ remaining counted as DC sales.
Non-GAAP GM (ex-SBC and charges) rose in Oct-Q, it came in at 73.6% vs. Citi’s 74%. Non-GAAP operating expenses (ex-SBC) were \$4.2B (ex-SBC), up 11% QoQ. Non-GAAP EPS (ex-SBC and charges) was \$1.30 up 24% QoQ.

Data center growth, yet again, is expected to be the primary driver of the sequential sales growth backed notably by the growing Gen AI demand of AI GPUs and networking products particularly NVDA’s Ethernet platform. Finally, NVDA is guiding GM to grow further with Jan-Q’s Non-GAAP GM (ex-SBC) reaching 75% (at MP), which is in line with Citi and Street expectations. The key driver of GM growth is Blackwell (in NVL form) now shipping at high volumes. This is coupled with the suspension of H20 which is a below-corporate-level-margins product. In-line with company guidance, we are subsequently modeling GM to remain relatively flat at 75%.

Following recent news around AI capex and projects we also revised our Accelerator TAM model. In terms of units… We model AI merchant GPUs to represent the larger mix of AI accelerators throughout C2025E to C2028E. We now expect merchant units to grow at a CAGR 27% vs the prior 25% during that period driven by demand NVDA but also AMD’s (covered by Chris Danely) recent win with Open AI. We nevertheless still suspect NVDA will continue to capture the bulk of AI accelerators investment due to its technology leadership and large installed base. Coming from a smaller base, we expect ASIC units to grow at a CAGR of 46% as various ASIC programs come online particularly in the 2027 timeframe. Combining the two, we expect AI accelerators to grow at a 34% CAGR between C2025E and C2028E. NVIDIA Corp (NVDA.O) 20 November 2025 Citi Research 7

In terms of compute sales… We expect the mix of AI merchant GPUs to remain high (from 90% in C2025E to 81% in C2028E). This is despite the expectation of lower merchant unit growth vs. ASICs. The primary reason for AI merchant GPUs sales shares remaining at 81%+ is the significantly higher merchant GPU ASPs (between 3x and 8x vs. ASICs). We model AI merchant GPUs sales to grow at a 28% CAGR vs. ASICs’ 66% over the next 3 years to reach \$403B and \$97B, respectively. We expect the combined TAM to grow at a 33% CAGR for a total of \$500B by C2028E vs. our prior \$464B forecast.

NVIDIA Corp
Company description
Nvidia is a leader in graphics processing units or GPUs. It is engaged in creating graphics and networking chips, which are used in gaming, data centers, and automotive end markets. Nvidia was founded by Jen-Hsun Huang (current CEO) and partners in January 1993 and is headquartered in Santa Clara, CA.
Investment strategy
We like Buy-rated NVDA on secular AI growth opportunities.
Valuation
Our price target for NVDA of \$270 is based on \~30x P/E on C27E earnings power of \$10 discounted back. Our 30x P/E multiple is in-line with 3-5 year average.
Risks
Downside risks to the attainment of our target price include: 1) competition on gaming could drive the stock lower if Nvidia loses market share; 2) slowerthan-expected adoption of new platforms can drive lower data center and gaming sales; 3) lumpiness in auto and data center markets can add volatility to the stock/multiple; and 4) cryptomining impact on gaming sales.

Guide to Citi Research Fundamental Research Investment Ratings: Citi Research stock recommendations include an investment rating and an optional risk rating to highlight high risk stocks. Risk rating takes into account both price volatility and fundamental criteria. Stocks will either have no risk rating or a High risk rating assigned. Investment Ratings: Citi Research investment ratings are Buy, Neutral and Sell. Our ratings are a function of analyst expectations of expected total return ("ETR") and risk. ETR is the sum of the forecast price appreciation (or depreciation) plus the dividend yield for a stock within the next 12 months. The target price is based on a 12 month time horizon. The Investment rating definitions are: Buy (1) ETR of 15% or more or 25% or more for High risk stocks; and Sell (3) for negative ETR. Any covered stock not assigned a Buy or a Sell is a Neutral (2). For stocks rated Neutral (2), if an analyst believes that there are insufficient valuation drivers and/or investment catalysts to derive a positive or negative investment view, they may elect with the approval of Citi Research management not to assign a target price and, thus, not derive an ETR. Citi Research may suspend its rating and target price and assign “Rating Suspended” status for regulatory and/or internal policy reasons. Citi Research may also suspend its rating and target price and assign "Under Review" status for other exceptional circumstances (e.g. lack of information critical to the analyst's thesis, trading suspension) affecting the company and/or trading in the company's NVIDIA Corp (NVDA.O) 20 November 2025 Citi Research 13

Catalyst Watch and STV Upside/Downside calls: Citi Research may also include a Catalyst Watch or STV Upside or Downside call to indicate the analyst expects the share price to rise (fall) in absolute terms over a specified period of 30 or 90 days in reaction to one or more specific near-term catalysts or events impacting the company or the market. A Catalyst Watch will be published when Analyst confidence is high that an impact to share price will occur; it will be a STV when confidence level is moderate. A Catalyst Watch or STV Upside/Downside call will automatically expire at the end of the specified 30/90 day period. The Catalyst Watch will also be automatically removed if share price performance (calculated at market close) exceeds 15% against the direction of the call (unless over-ridden by the analyst). The analyst may also remove a Catalyst Watch or STV call prior to the end of the specified period in a published research note. A Catalyst Watch/STV Upside or Downside call may be different from and does not affect a stock’s fundamental equity rating, which reflects a longer-term total absolute return expectation. For purposes of FINRA ratings-distribution-disclosure rules, a Catalyst Watch/STV Upside call corresponds to a buy recommendation and a Catalyst Watch/STV Downside call corresponds to a sell recommendation. Any stock not assigned to a Catalyst Watch Upside, Catalyst Watch Downside, STV Upside, or STV Downside call is considered Catalyst Watch/STV No View. For purposes of FINRA ratings distribution-disclosure rules, we correspond Catalyst Watch/STV No View to Hold in our ratings distribution table for our Catalyst Watch/STV Upside/Downside rating system. However, we reiterate that we do not consider No View to be a recommendation. For all Catalyst Watch/STV Upside/Downside calls, risk exists that the catalyst(s) and associated share-price movement will not materialize as expected.
